children: U.S. ethanol stocks edged up last week with production of the fuel unchanged from the week before, according to data released Wednesday by the U.S. Energy Information Administration.
Ethanol stocks increased by 33,000 barrels to 25.22 million barrels in the week ended Sept. 11, the EIA said. Production held steady at 1.099 million barrels a day.

Production estimates among analysts surveyed by Dow Jones ranged from 1.080 million barrels a day to 1.104 million barrels a day. Ethanol inventory estimates ranged from 24.5 million barrels to 25.4 million barrels.
The U.S. had record-high ethanol exports in 2024 and 2025, with further increases in the first half of this year, the Department of Agriculture said in a report Tuesday.

The principal driver was growing import demand in the largest consuming markets, the USDA said. The U.S. exported 1.9 billion gallons of ethanol worth $4.3 billion in 2024, and 2.2 billion gallons worth $4.7 billion in 2025. Through June of 2026, exports were up 12% by volume and 21% by value.
